jobs.title: Chief People Officer
jobs.description:
Department:
People & Culture

Location:
British Columbia, Canada (Hybrid)

Description

Photonic is building the world’s first commercial-scale quantum computer, and we are growing fast to do it. We are seeking an exceptional Chief People Officer (CPO)
to serve as the CEO’s trusted partner and a leading voice on the executive team, shaping the decisions that determine who we hire, how we lead, how we reward, and how ready we are when investors, acquirers, or public markets look closely. This is not a back-office seat. It is a seat at the table for someone who can influence at the top, move quickly, and build. This role is based in Coquitlam, BC, with 2–3 days per week in the office.

Please include a cover letter with your resume (in one file) describing how you would be a great fit at Photonic and what attributes you could bring to our growing team.

What We Need You To Do

Executive Partnership & Influence

Act as the CEO’s thought partner on company strategy, organizational design, and the people decisions that shape Photonic’s trajectory.
Represent people and culture in the boardroom, advising the Board and its committees on executive compensation, succession, and talent risk.
Advise and coach the executive team through growth, transformation, and high-stakes decisions with candour and credibility.
Translate business strategy into a multi-year workforce plan, and give leadership the insight to act on it.

Talent Acquisition & Leadership Pipeline

Set the strategy for winning highly specialized scientific and engineering talent (PhDs, quantum, photonics) in a fiercely competitive global market.
Build the leadership bench and succession pipeline that will carry Photonic through its next stages of growth, and protect our promote-from-within culture.
Establish Photonic as a global employer of choice for the people who will build the future of computing.

Compensation, Benefits & Total Rewards

Define a global rewards philosophy across Canada, the US, and the UK that attracts and retains world-class talent.
Steward equity and executive compensation strategy so it is competitive, defensible, and built to withstand investor and acquirer due diligence.
Partner with the CEO and CFO to align people investment with financial strategy.

Organizational Readiness & Governance

Build the people governance and compliance framework that a company under investor, acquirer, or public-market scrutiny is expected to have.
Anticipate and manage people-related risk, including employment, regulatory, and reputational risk, as we expand globally.
Ensure our people infrastructure scales ahead of the business as headcount accelerates.

Culture & Organizational Leadership

Champion a culture rooted in our values of Fearless Ambition, Accountability, Growth, and Respect as we scale across borders.
Build and lead a high-performing HR organization across talent acquisition, HR operations, total rewards, and business partnership.
Own the strategy for engagement, performance, and retention, and hold leaders accountable for results.

What You Bring To Our Team

15+ years of progressive HR leadership, including at least 5 years leading an HR function at the senior leadership level in a scaling technology or deep tech environment.
Bachelor’s degree in HR, BA, or a related field, with an MBA or equivalent advanced degree. CPHR designation or equivalent (e.g., SHRM-SCP, CIPD). A combination of education and senior executive experience will be considered.
A proven trusted advisor to CEOs and boards, with the executive presence and judgment to match.
Proven ability to build and scale HR processes and teams through periods of rapid growth (100→500+ employees).
A strategic, enterprise-level thinker who connects people decisions to business outcomes and investor expectations.
Experience leading HR across multiple geographies (Canada required; US and/or UK strongly preferred).
Strong knowledge of Canadian employment law; familiarity with US and UK employment regulations is a significant asset.
Strong command of Canadian employment law and the judgment to navigate complex, sensitive matters with discretion.
Comfortable with the pace, ambiguity, and shifting priorities of a company at this stage of growth.
A bias to action and a genuine love of building.
A fit with our values: Fearless Ambition, Accountability, Growth, and Respect.

An Exceptional Candidate Will Bring

Experience scaling an organization through rapid growth (100→500+ employees) and preparing it for investor, acquirer, or public-market scrutiny.
Experience leading organizational design and change through a transition from research to commercialization.
Experience advising a Board or its compensation committee, including equity strategy.
Working knowledge of US and UK employment frameworks.

WHY YOU SHOULD WORK WITH US

Work closely with some of the brightest innovators in quantum technologies to drive breakthroughs that redefine computing
Join at a pivotal moment and help shape and lead an organization through one of the most exciting phases a company can experience
Inclusive company culture that values collaboration
Clear career paths, with 80% of our managers and directors promoted from within
Regular social events and fun activities keep our global team connected
Competitive compensation package including base salary, stock options, and relocation assistance for global talent
Comprehensive benefits including extended health, dental, life, long term disability, an employee assistance program, parental leave top-ups, a flexible spending account, and unlimited wellness leave

The description above is what we think an ideal candidate would look like for this role. At Photonic, we understand that everyone has a different work and life journey. If you feel your experience is close to what we've described, but you might not meet all the requirements, please still apply! We are also committed to fostering, cultivating, and preserving a culture of equity, diversity, and inclusion. We embrace and encourage our employees’ differences, knowing that these very differences inspire innovation and build better teams. If there are any accommodations our team can make throughout our hiring process, please let us know.

jobs.title: Account Director
jobs.description:
Job Title:- Account Director

Work Type:- Full-Time

Work Mode:- Hybrid

Tru Inc. is hiring an Account Director for an immediate permanent opportunity. This is a senior, client-facing role for someone who has already carried a portfolio of this size and sat across the table from a client executive team.

Position Overview:-

The Account Director owns the full client lifecycle for a $3M to $5M account portfolio, serving as an executive advisor to clients and a strategic partner to internal teams. This role leads digital growth strategies across CRM, marketing automation, commerce, analytics, and related enterprise platforms. The Account Director reports to Client Services leadership.

Location:-

This is a hybrid role with some work-from-home flexibility. Preference will be given to candidates in the Greater Toronto Area, as the role follows a three-day-per-week in-office schedule to support collaboration, workshops, and client engagement. Travel to client and partner offices is required.

The Accounts You’ll Own:-

What separates this role from our Account Manager role is the size and complexity of the accounts, not the seniority of the people in the room. Account Directors carry Tru’s most complex clients:
Scale:
Enterprise accounts and multi-workstream programmes, typically $500K+ in annual value each, totalling a $3M to $5M portfolio across 6-8 relationships.
Complexity:
Three or more concurrent workstreams per account, frequently with separate budgets, separate executive sponsors, and dependencies between them.
Client organization:
Matrixed enterprises where several executives hold competing priorities, and where procurement, IT, security, and brand each have a say in what ships.
Horizon:
Multi-year programmes where the roadmap outlives any individual project, and where this year’s decisions constrain next year’s options.

Core Responsibilities:-

Portfolio Management:
Own and grow 6-8 high-value client relationships, maintaining a $3M to $5M portfolio benchmark while managing budgets, contracts, invoicing, performance, satisfaction, and escalations.
Executive Advisory & Alignment:
Build trusted relationships across a matrixed client executive group, translating competing business priorities into a single actionable digital transformation plan.
Strategic Lifecycle Planning:
Lead Quarterly Business Reviews and develop multi-year marketing and technology roadmaps aligned to measurable client outcomes.
Cross-Functional Delivery:
Partner with engineering, marketing, and delivery teams to define scope, milestones, budgets, and timelines across concurrent workstreams.
Commercial Strategy:
Own portfolio-level commercial direction: multi-year agreements, rate and pricing negotiation, commercial exceptions, and margin across the full portfolio.
Commercial Growth:
Collaborate with Business Development and Client Services leadership to shape proposals, expand accounts, and decide where Tru invests for profitable growth.
Escalation Ownership:
Act as the named escalation point for the portfolio, resolving delivery, commercial, and relationship risk before it reaches leadership.
Capability Development:
Mentor Account Managers and set the standard for client-facing practice. The Account Director group is where Tru develops its next account leaders.
Operational Discipline:
Maintain CRM accuracy and pipeline health in HubSpot to support transparent reporting, resource forecasting, and account risk management.

Technical Platform Ecosystem:-

The Account Director should bring strong conceptual and architectural awareness of enterprise technology platforms to guide client roadmaps across these areas:
Enterprise CRM & Automation:
Use Salesforce and related platforms to improve lead generation, audience data management, engagement tracking, and pipeline efficiency.
Digital Experience & Content:
Advise on Adobe Experience Cloud and CMS initiatives that create consistent customer experiences across web, mobile, and digital channels.
Composable Commerce:
Guide API-first and headless commerce strategies, including CommerceTools, to support flexible and scalable digital storefronts.
Data Analytics & Insights:
Use analytics platforms, including Google Analytics, to track performance, build reporting models, and recommend data-backed optimizations.
Search & Performance Marketing:
Advise on SEO, AEO, and paid media strategy and campaign activations and optimizations.

This role advises on platform direction; it does not configure or build. Hands-on certification is welcome but not required.

What You’ll Bring:-

Professional Experience:
6 to 9 years of progressive experience in strategic account management, technology consulting, digital marketing, or enterprise agency environments.
Portfolio Scale:
Demonstrated ownership of client relationships at $1M+ in individual annual value, or a portfolio at $3M+, with the results to show for it.
Enterprise Complexity:
Experience inside matrixed client organizations where several sponsors hold competing priorities and no single person can approve a direction alone. Managing a senior relationship at a smaller, simpler account is valuable experience, but it is not the same job.
Commercial Authority:
A track record negotiating multi-year agreements, rates, and commercial exceptions, with accountability for margin as well as revenue.
Technical Fluency:
Experience managing enterprise-scale web applications, cloud solutions, systems integrations, or digital platforms.
Executive Communication:
Strong business analysis, storytelling, negotiation, and stakeholder-management skills for senior and C-suite audiences.
Client Advocacy:
Ability to navigate matrixed client organizations and turn ambiguous requirements into structured delivery plans.
Solution Orientation:
A results-driven mindset focused on delivering value, strengthening client relationships, and exceeding expectations.
Education:
Bachelor’s degree preferred in Marketing, Information Technology, Business Administration, or a related field.

Salary Range:- $100,000- $120,000

Where This Role Leads:-

Account Director is not the top of the ladder at Tru. The path continues into client engagement leadership — holding a group of accounts rather than a portfolio, developing the Account Directors who run them, and carrying commercial accountability at the practice level rather than the account level. Account Directors who grow their portfolio and build the next group of account leaders are the people we develop into that role.

Working at Tru:-

At Tru, we put people first. We offer competitive salaries, a 100% employer-paid benefits package, and a hybrid work arrangement. Our culture is grounded in courage, entrepreneurship, diversity, and a passion for people, supported by regular team events and live gatherings that build connection beyond day-to-day work.
Our values are:-
You Talk, We Listen

Integrity at Our Core

Quality as Standard

Delivered On Time

Join Tru and help clients make measurable progress across the digital platforms that power their growth.

Director

Full-time

IT Services and IT Consulting

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
At Albert College, strong financial leadership helps make an exceptional education possible. Located in Belleville, Ontario, Albert is a CAIS-accredited, Pre-Kindergarten to Grade 12 day and boarding school where students from Canada and around the world thrive in a close-knit community. Our commitment to Academics, Arts, Athletics, Active Citizenship, and Adventure inspires the development of courageous global citizens. With exciting opportunities ahead, we are seeking a Chief Financial Officer who wants to help shape the next chapter of our school.

Reporting to the Head of School, the Chief Financial Officer is a key member of the Senior Leadership Team and an ex-officio member of the Board of Governors. More than a steward of the books, the CFO is a trusted strategic partner, offering clear financial insight to support the College’s priorities and sustainability. The role leads financial planning, budgeting, financial reporting, investments, audits, enterprise risk management and compliance, while providing leadership for facilities, human resources, health and safety, food services, information technology, and transportation. The CFO works closely with the Head of School, Board and colleagues to turn ambitious plans into sound, actionable decisions.

We are looking for a thoughtful, collaborative leader with a CPA designation, an undergraduate degree, and at least five years of experience in financial management, including experience in a leadership role. The ideal candidate combines technical expertise and sound judgment with the ability to see the bigger picture, communicate complex financial information clearly and inspire confidence across a diverse school community. Experience with not-for-profit governance, the financial aspects of fundraising, and developing new revenue opportunities would be an asset. Above all, we are looking for someone who leads with integrity, values relationships, and believes in the impact of education.

Why Albert College?
You will join a warm, highly collaborative community that takes pride in its students and its mission, with a genuine opportunity to influence the school’s future. We offer a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits, participation in the Albert College pension plan, generous vacation and holidays, and tuition remission for eligible children.

Salary:

$145,000 - 165,000 annually

Anticipated Start Date:
April 2027, although a flexible start date may be considered for the successful candidate.

To see a detailed job description, please visit albertcollege.ca/about/careers/

To apply:
Please submit a cover letter and résumé in confidence to:

Mark Musca, Head of School, Albert College
160 Dundas Street West, Belleville, Ontario K8P 1A6
jobposting@albertcollege.ca

Albert College is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to inclusive, barrier-free recruitment and selection processes. We welcome applications from Indigenous peoples, persons with disabilities, visible minorities, and persons of all sexual orientations and gender identities. Please contact us if you require this posting in an alternate format. If contacted for an employment opportunity, please advise us if you require accommodation, and we will work with you to meet your needs. We thank all applicants for their interest in this position; however, only those applicants selected for an interview will be contacted. AI is not used for screening purposes.

jobs.company: The Clarice Smith Performing Arts Center
jobs.title: Executive Director, The Clarice Smith Performing Arts Center
jobs.location: Urban agglomeration of Montreal, Quebec, Canada
jobs.description:
APPLICATION DEADLINE

November 13, 2026, for Best Consideration

POSITION

Staff Regular

SALARY RANGE

$235,000-$275,000

The Clarice Overview

The Clarice Smith Performing Arts Center (The Clarice) at the University of Maryland (UMD) is part of the College of Arts and Humanities (ARHU) and is the academic and artistic home of the School of Music (SOM); the School of Theatre, Dance, and Performance Studies (TDPS); the Michelle Smith Performing Arts Library (MSPAL); and The Clarice’s own artistic platform Clarice Presents (CP). At the time of its construction, the 318,000-square-foot facility on 17 acres of land was the largest construction project undertaken by the State of Maryland, and remains one of the most complex projects in recent Maryland state history.

The Clarice opened in 2001 and is named in honor of visual artist and philanthropist Clarice Smith (1933-2021). From its founding, The Clarice was conceived as a “creative village” that brought a robust series of outside artists and performers to campus, supported the academic and performance programs of SOM and TDPS and collaborations with MSPAL, and built bridges between UMD and its surrounding community. The Clarice, through its dynamic outreach programs, manifested UMD’s commitment to meaningfully contribute to those communities through the arts and the encouragement of cultural citizenship. The Clarice continues to strengthen its role as the central home for performing arts at UMD, supporting the academic and performance needs of SOM and TDPS, ensuring the excellence and social relevance of all of its programs, and enhancing its leadership position in the field despite the political and financial headwinds for the arts in this country.

The Clarice hosts more than 1,000 public performances and events each year, the majority featuring the artistry of SOM and TDPS students and faculty. The Clarice’s artistic platform, Clarice Presents (CP), offers uniquely integrated performances, digital, civic and community engagement programming. MSPAL, often in partnership with CP and M‐NCPPC, also presents events at The Clarice. All presentations and events are supported by the administrative, production management, and technical staff of The Clarice.

Professional staff across artistic planning, operations, and finance report to the Executive Director, who works in close collaboration with College senior leadership, academic partners, and marketing, communication, and development staff.

Position Summary/Purpose

Reporting directly to the Dean of the College of Arts and Humanities, the Executive Director is ultimately responsible for the management of The Clarice’s staff, operations, facilities, budget, and fundraising. In these roles, the position balances educational, public, and financial priorities to ensure that operations and programming simultaneously enhance The Clarice’s stature as a national leader among performing arts presenters and contribute meaningfully to the resident academic units’ missions; reflect the values of collaboration, belonging, and community; and align with the goals of the college and institution. In collaboration with the Directors of the resident academic units, the position is responsible for the Clarice’s artistic programming and works to ensure that this programming and other initiatives respond to curricular needs. The Executive Director works alongside Directors of the School of Music; the School of Theatre, Dance, and Performance Studies; and the Michelle Smith Performing Arts Library, as well as the Executive Director of Arts for All to develop and refine a strategic and innovative vision that enhances the curricular experience for faculty and students, engages the campus, connects with the community, and further enhances the reputation of the University of Maryland. The Executive Director should bring significant knowledge of the changing performing arts landscape and a fierce dedication to collaborative leadership models. The Executive Director meets monthly with the Dean and annually with the Provost and Dean to ensure that the performing arts have a campus and community-wide agenda and impact. For more detailed information about The Clarice please visit this website.

Minimum Qualifications

Education: Bachelor’s degree from accredited college or University.
Experience: Twelve (12) years of professional experience, including at least six (6) years supervising or managing professional staff.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage and inspire stakeholders at all levels.
Ability to make sound decisions, solve complex problems, and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Knowledge of relevant industry regulations and best practices.

Apply

Required application materials: Resume, Cover Letter, List of References

Learn more about UMD, The Clarice and campus partners.

Apply now

The Clarice Overview

The Clarice Smith Performing Arts Center (The Clarice) at the University of Maryland (UMD) is part of the College of Arts and Humanities (ARHU) and is the academic and artistic home of the School of Music (SOM); the School of Theatre, Dance, and Performance Studies (TDPS); the Michelle Smith Performing Arts Library (MSPAL); and The Clarice’s own artistic platform Clarice Presents (CP). At the time of its construction, the 318,000-square-foot facility on 17 acres of land was the largest construction project undertaken by the State of Maryland, and remains one of the most complex projects in recent Maryland state history.

The Clarice opened in 2001 and is named in honor of visual artist and philanthropist Clarice Smith (1933-2021). From its founding, The Clarice was conceived as a “creative village” that brought a robust series of outside artists and performers to campus, supported the academic and performance programs of SOM and TDPS and collaborations with MSPAL, and built bridges between UMD and its surrounding community. The Clarice, through its dynamic outreach programs, manifested UMD’s commitment to meaningfully contribute to those communities through the arts and the encouragement of cultural citizenship. The Clarice continues to strengthen its role as the central home for performing arts at UMD, supporting the academic and performance needs of SOM and TDPS, ensuring the excellence and social relevance of all of its programs, and enhancing its leadership position in the field despite the political and financial headwinds for the arts in this country.

The Clarice hosts more than 1,000 public performances and events each year, the majority featuring the artistry of SOM and TDPS students and faculty. The Clarice’s artistic platform, Clarice Presents (CP), offers uniquely integrated performances, digital, civic and community engagement programming. MSPAL, often in partnership with CP and M‐NCPPC, also presents events at The Clarice. All presentations and events are supported by the administrative, production management, and technical staff of The Clarice.

Professional staff across artistic planning, operations, and finance report to the Executive Director, who works in close collaboration with College senior leadership, academic partners, and marketing, communication, and development staff.

Position Summary/Purpose

Reporting directly to the Dean of the College of Arts and Humanities, the Executive Director is ultimately responsible for the management of The Clarice’s staff, operations, facilities, budget, and fundraising. In these roles, the position balances educational, public, and financial priorities to ensure that operations and programming simultaneously enhance The Clarice’s stature as a national leader among performing arts presenters and contribute meaningfully to the resident academic units’ missions; reflect the values of collaboration, belonging, and community; and align with the goals of the college and institution. In collaboration with the Directors of the resident academic units, the position is responsible for the Clarice’s artistic programming and works to ensure that this programming and other initiatives respond to curricular needs. The Executive Director works alongside Directors of the School of Music; the School of Theatre, Dance, and Performance Studies; and the Michelle Smith Performing Arts Library, as well as the Executive Director of Arts for All to develop and refine a strategic and innovative vision that enhances the curricular experience for faculty and students, engages the campus, connects with the community, and further enhances the reputation of the University of Maryland. The Executive Director should bring significant knowledge of the changing performing arts landscape and a fierce dedication to collaborative leadership models. The Executive Director meets monthly with the Dean and annually with the Provost and Dean to ensure that the performing arts have a campus and community-wide agenda and impact. For more detailed information about The Clarice please visit this website.

Minimum Qualifications

Education: Bachelor’s degree from accredited college or University.
Experience: Twelve (12) years of professional experience, including at least six (6) years supervising or managing professional staff.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage and inspire stakeholders at all levels.
Ability to make sound decisions, solve complex problems, and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Knowledge of relevant industry regulations and best practices.
